drivingQuestion: Why is one who says 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest' silenced?
outcomeNote: Two reasons for silencing the bird's-nest prayer are supplied by the Western amoraim without deciding between them; the difficulty from Rabba's praise is resolved (he meant to sharpen Abaye); R' Ḥanina's rebuke stands as a teaching against adding praises.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ בִּשְׁלָמָא, ״מוֹדִים, מוֹדִים״ מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ — מִשּׁוּם דְּמֶיחְזֵי כִּשְׁתֵּי רָשׁוּיוֹת. וְ״עַל טוֹב יִזָּכֵר שְׁמֶךָ״ נָמֵי, מַשְׁמַע עַל הַטּוֹבָה וְלֹא עַל הָרָעָה, וּתְנַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה. אֶלָּא ״עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ״ מַאי טַעְמָא?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» Our mishna cited three instances where the communal prayer leader is silenced. The Gemara clarifies: «Granted,» they silence one who repeats: «We give thanks, we give thanks, as it appears like» he is acknowledging and praying to «two authorities. And» granted that «they also silence» one who says: «May Your name be mentioned with the good,» as «clearly» he is thanking God only «for the good and not for the bad, and we learned» in a mishna: «One is required to bless» God «for the bad just as he blesses» Him «for the good. However,» in the case of one who recites: Just as «Your mercy is extended to a bird’s nest, why» do they silence him?

segments.he: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי בְּמַעְרְבָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא: חַד אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמֵּטִיל קִנְאָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית. וְחַד אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רַחֲמִים, וְאֵינָן אֶלָּא גְּזֵרוֹת.
segments.en: «Two amora’im in Eretz Yisrael disputed this» question; «Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida; one said» that this was «because he engenders jealousy among God’s creations,» as it appears as though he is protesting the fact that the Lord favored one creature over all others. «And one said» that this was «because he transforms the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, into» expressions of «mercy, when they are nothing but decrees» of the King that must be fulfilled without inquiring into the reasons behind them.

segments.he: הַהוּא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה וַאֲמַר: אַתָּה חַסְתָּ עַל קַן צִפּוֹר, אַתָּה חוּס וְרַחֵם עָלֵינוּ. אֲמַר רַבָּה: כַּמָּה יָדַע הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנָן לְרַצּוֹיֵי לְמָרֵיהּ! אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ תְּנַן!
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «a particular» individual «descended before the ark» as prayer leader «in the presence of Rabba, and said» in his prayers: «You have shown mercy to the bird’s nest, now have mercy and pity upon us. Rabba said: How much does this Torah scholar know to appease» the Lord, «his Master. Abaye said to him: Didn’t we learn» in a mishna that «they silence him?»

segments.he: וְרַבָּה נָמֵי, לְחַדּוֹדֵי אַבָּיֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «And Rabba too» held in accordance with this mishna but merely acted this way because «he wanted to hone Abaye’s» intellect. Rabba did not make his statement to praise the scholar, but simply to test his nephew, Abaye, and to encourage him to articulate what he knows about that mishna.

segments.he: הַהוּא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אֲמַר ״הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא וְהָאַדִּיר וְהָעִזּוּז וְהַיָּראוּי, הֶחָזָק וְהָאַמִּיץ וְהַוַּדַּאי וְהַנִּכְבָּד״.
segments.en: With regard to additions to prayers formulated by the Sages, The Gemara relates that «a particular» individual «descended before the ark» as prayer leader «in the presence of Rabbi Ḥanina.» He extended his prayer and «said: God, the great, mighty, awesome, powerful, mighty, awe-inspiring, strong, fearless, steadfast and honored.»

segments.he: הִמְתִּין לוֹ עַד דְּסַיֵּים. כִּי סַיֵּים אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סַיֵּימְתִּינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ שִׁבְחֵי דְמָרָךְ?! לְמָה לִי כּוּלֵּי הַאי? אֲנַן, הָנֵי תְּלָת דְּאָמְרִינַן אִי לָאו דְּאַמְרִינְהוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וַאֲתוֹ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה וְתַקְּנִינְהוּ בִּתְפִלָּה — לָא הֲוֵינַן יְכוֹלִין לְמֵימַר לְהוּ, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי וְאָזְלַתְּ! מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ אֶלֶף אֲלָפִים דִּינְרֵי זָהָב, וְהָיוּ מְקַלְּסִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשֶׁל כֶּסֶף. וַהֲלֹא גְּנַאי הוּא לוֹ!
segments.en: Rabbi Ḥanina «waited for him until he completed» his prayer. «When he finished,» Rabbi Ḥanina «asked him: Have you concluded all of the praises of your Master? Why do I need all of this» superfluous praise? «Even these three» praises «that we recite:» The great, mighty and awesome, «had Moses our teacher not said them in the Torah and had the members of the Great Assembly not come and incorporated them into the» Amida prayer, «we would not be permitted to recite them. And you went on and recited all of these. It is comparable to a king who possessed many thousands of golden dinars, yet they were praising him for silver» ones. «Isn’t that deprecatory?» All of the praises we could possibly lavish upon the Lord are nothing but a few silver dinars relative to many thousands of gold dinars. Reciting a litany of praise does not enhance God’s honor.

moves.summary: grants the reasons for the first two clauses of the mishna: 'modim, modim' looks like two authorities; 'for the good' implies not for the bad
moves.about: the reasons behind the mishna's first two clauses: 'modim, modim' looks like acknowledging two authorities; 'for the good' implies thanking only for good and not for bad

moves.cueHe: ותנן: חייב אדם לברך על הרעה
moves.summary: cites the mishna that one must bless for the bad as for the good, supporting the second reason
moves.about: the mishna requiring one to bless God for the bad as for the good, supporting the reason for silencing 'for the good may Your name be mentioned'

moves.cueHe: אלא ״על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך״ מאי טעמא
moves.summary: asks why the bird's-nest prayer warrants silencing
moves.about: why one who says 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest' is silenced, given that the other two clauses of the mishna have evident reasons

moves.summary: reports that two Western amoraim, R' Yosei bar Avin and R' Yosei bar Zevida, dispute the reason
moves.about: the reason one who says 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest' is silenced: because he casts jealousy among the works of creation, or because he makes God's attributes mercy when they are only decrees

moves.cueHe: חד אמר: מפני שמטיל קנאה במעשה בראשית
moves.summary: one of the two: because he casts jealousy among the works of creation
moves.about: the reason for silencing the bird's-nest prayer — he supplies one of the two reasons (jealousy in creation / attributes as decrees); 'חד אמר' leaves which one his undetermined

moves.cueHe: וחד אמר: מפני שעושה מדותיו של הקדוש ברוך הוא רחמים
moves.summary: the other: because he makes God's attributes mercy when they are only decrees
moves.about: the reason for silencing the bird's-nest prayer — he supplies one of the two reasons (jealousy in creation / attributes as decrees); 'חד אמר' leaves which one his undetermined

moves.summary: a prayer leader before Rabba prays: as You had mercy on the bird's nest, have mercy on us
moves.about: an individual descends before the ark as prayer leader in Rabba's presence and prays 'as You had mercy on the bird's nest, have mercy on us'

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה: כמה ידע האי צורבא מרבנן לרצויי למריה
moves.summary: Rabba praises the leader for knowing how to appease his Master
moves.about: the prayer leader's skill in appeasing his Master with the bird's-nest formulation (said, the gemara later explains, to sharpen Abaye)

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: והא משתקין אותו תנן
moves.summary: Abaye objects from the mishna: such a leader is silenced
moves.about: whether the bird's-nest prayer can be praised when the mishna rules that its reciter is silenced

moves.cueHe: ורבה נמי, לחדודי אביי הוא דבעי
moves.summary: Rabba too agrees with the mishna; he spoke only to sharpen Abaye
moves.about: Rabba too accepts the mishna's ruling; he praised the leader only in order to sharpen Abaye

moves.summary: a prayer leader before R' Ḥanina recites ten epithets of God
moves.about: an individual descends before the ark as prayer leader in R' Ḥanina's presence and recites ten epithets of God

moves.cueHe: כי סיים אמר ליה: סיימתינהו לכולהו שבחי דמרך
moves.summary: R' Ḥanina rebukes the additions: even the three epithets are said only because Moses said them and the Great Assembly fixed them
moves.about: heaping praises on God beyond the three epithets that Moses said and the Men of the Great Assembly fixed in prayer; parable of praising a king of gold in silver

moves.summary: parable: praising a king who has thousands of gold dinars for silver ones is a disgrace
